notes.meaning: Jesus declares that a new time has arrived when spiritually dead people will hear His voice and receive life. When someone hears the gospel and believes in the Son of God, Christ's voice awakens their heart from the deadness of sin. This shows that true spiritual life comes only through hearing and trusting Jesus.

differ.view: Christ is not speaking of all the dead indiscriminately, but only of the elect whose ears God pierces and opens by His Spirit to receive life.
This hearing is an effectual awakening worked by God's grace in the believing heart, displaying Jesus' sovereign power over death.

notes.meaning: God the Father has life entirely within Himself, not depending on anyone else for His existence. He has granted this exact same power to Jesus the Son, who possesses the fullness of life to impart to others. Because of this divine gift, Jesus has full authority to give spiritual life to all who come to Him.

The Father has given Jesus the authority to act as Judge over the entire world because He is the Son of Man. Because Jesus took on human nature, He understands our weaknesses firsthand and is perfectly suited to judge mankind fairly. We can take comfort knowing our final Judge is completely righteous and knows our human frame.

Jesus tells His hearers not to be amazed, because a day is coming when all the physically dead in their graves will hear His call. Everyone will come out of the dust to appear before His judgment seat, where those who did good will rise to eternal life and those who did evil will face condemnation. Our daily lives will openly reveal whether our faith in God was genuine.

differ.view: Good works do not earn eternal life, but they serve as the necessary fruit that distinguishes true believers from the condemned.

notes.meaning: Jesus explains that He never acts independently or for selfish reasons, but works in complete harmony with the Father. His judgments are always fair and true because His only desire is to carry out the will of the One who sent Him. We find our own truest guidance by surrendering our wills to God's direction.

Under the law, a person's testimony about himself was not accepted as legal proof in court. Jesus does not say His claims are untrue, but He recognizes that human courts require supporting witnesses to establish the truth. He therefore sets aside His own word alone and points to other witnesses to prove who He is.

Jesus points to another witness whose testimony can never be questioned, meaning God the Father. Jesus is completely confident that the Father's witness concerning Him is true and beyond reproach. Believers can rest their faith on the sure testimony of God Himself.

The religious leaders had sent an official group of priests to question John the Baptist out in the wilderness. When questioned, John told them the honest truth and pointed directly to Jesus as the Messiah. The leaders had sought out John's testimony themselves, and it stood as a clear witness against their unbelief.

Jesus does not depend on human praise or human testimony to validate His divine mission, because God's word is far greater than human words. He mentions John's witness only because He wants His hearers to be convinced and saved. Even when dealing with critics, Jesus' heart is set on their salvation.

John the Baptist was like a lamp that burned with zeal and shone with clear spiritual light to guide a dark generation. The Jewish leaders were glad to enjoy his popularity for a short time like an exciting novelty. However, their interest was shallow, and they quickly turned away when his preaching confronted their sins.

Jesus possesses a witness that is far greater and more convincing than John the Baptist. The miracles and saving works that the Father gave Him to finish prove that God truly sent Him. These mighty deeds could only be performed by divine authority and power.

God the Father Himself has testified to Jesus through the ancient Scriptures and by speaking at His baptism. Yet the religious leaders had never truly listened to God's voice or known what He is like. Because they were spiritually blind to God, they failed to recognize His Son standing right in front of them.

Jesus tells the leaders that God's word has no real dwelling place in their hearts. If Scripture were truly living inside them, they would have welcomed Jesus, the One whom God sent. Our response to Jesus reveals whether God's truth has truly taken root in our souls.

The religious leaders painstakingly studied the Scriptures because they assumed that merely possessing and reading the Law earned them eternal life. Yet the whole purpose of the sacred writings was to point straight to Jesus as the Savior. Reading the Bible only brings life when it leads us to put our faith in Christ Himself.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Jesus is not giving a command to read the Bible, but describing the fact that the leaders studied the text hoping to earn life by it while missing its true meaning.

notes.meaning: Even though the Scriptures point directly to Jesus, the people obstinately refused to come to Him to receive eternal life. The issue was not that they lacked clear evidence, but that their proud wills refused to submit to Him. Christ offers life freely, but people perish when they choose not to come.

Jesus explains that He does not seek or need praise and applause from human beings. He did not come into the world to win popularity or build an earthly following. His only motive is the glory of God and the good of souls.

Jesus sees directly into their hearts and reveals their real condition: they had no true love for God. While they made a great show of being religious, their hearts were completely cold toward God's holiness and goodness. Outward religious activity is empty if it does not flow from a heart that loves the Lord.

Jesus came with the authority and backing of His heavenly Father, yet the leaders rejected Him. However, if a false teacher appears promoting his own name and seeking his own glory, people will eagerly follow him. When people shut their eyes to God's truth, they easily fall for dangerous deceptions.

Jesus asks how the leaders could ever believe while they were constantly trading honors and compliments with one another. Looking for praise from people makes genuine faith impossible, because it blinds the soul to the honor that comes from God alone. To follow Christ, we must desire God's approval more than human applause.

Jesus explains that He does not need to bring charges against them before the Father. Moses, the very prophet in whom they placed all their pride and hope, will stand as their accuser. The very law they relied on will expose their failure and condemn their stubborn unbelief.

If the leaders had genuinely believed what Moses taught, they would have welcomed Jesus without hesitation. Moses pointed to Christ throughout his writings, through direct prophecies, promises, and the ceremonies of the law. Rejecting Jesus proved that they never truly understood or believed Moses at all.

Since they refused to believe the written words of Moses, which they could read and examine every day, they could hardly be expected to believe Jesus' spoken message. Rejecting the foundation of God's ancient word leaves a person completely closed to current truth. Trusting what God has written prepares our hearts to welcome the words of Christ.
